title: The Hidden Bias of Process Reward Models:PRISM for Rewarding the Right Reasoning
title_zh: Process Reward Models 的隐藏偏差：PRISM 用正确理由奖励正确推理
abstract_en: Process Reward Models (PRMs) improve credit assignment for reasoning by providing step-level feedback. However, we identify a hidden bias in PRMs caused by severe imbalance in step-level training data. Standard cross-entropy training amplifies this bias, causing PRMs to overcredit plausible but incorrect steps and produce high false-positive rates. We show that these false positives have an asymmetric downstream effect: false negatives mainly slow exploration, whereas false positives actively steer Best-of-N selection, guided decoding, and policy optimization toward flawed reasoning. This suggests that PRM training should shift from pointwise label fitting to reliable relative comparisons. To address this, we propose PRISM (Precision Ranking for Improved Step Modeling), a policy-aware PRM training framework that learns from contrastive step-level comparisons and hard negatives generated by a temporal lookahead strategy, requiring no new human labels. We further use a difficulty-aware curriculum to optimize the contrastive step margin. Across PRMBench and ProcessBench, PRISM substantially reduces false positives (22% on PRMBench) and improves macro F1 over strong discriminative PRMs. When applied to policy optimization and search tasks, including guided decoding and Best-of-N selection, it consistently improves accuracy (up to 22% for guided decoding and 33% for Best-of-N) and robustness. More broadly, trustworthy process supervision is not just about assigning high rewards, but about rewarding the right reasoning for the right reasons.
abstract_zh: 本文指出，Process Reward Models（PRMs）虽然通过步骤级反馈改善推理任务中的 credit assignment，但其训练数据存在严重的步骤级类别不均衡，导致一种隐藏偏差。标准 cross-entropy 训练会放大该偏差，使 PRMs 容易给“看似合理但实际错误”的推理步骤过高奖励，从而产生较高 false-positive 率。作者进一步发现，false positive 与 false negative 对下游的影响并不对称：false negative 主要降低探索效率，而 false positive 会主动把 Best-of-N selection、guided decoding 和 policy optimization 引向错误推理。为此，论文提出 PRISM（Precision Ranking for Improved Step Modeling），一种 policy-aware 的 PRM 训练框架，通过对比式步骤级排序学习和 temporal lookahead 生成的 hard negatives 来训练模型，无需额外人工标注；同时引入 difficulty-aware curriculum 来优化对比学习中的步骤间隔。在 PRMBench 和 ProcessBench 上，PRISM 相比强判别式 PRMs 显著降低 false positives（PRMBench 上降低 22%）并提升 macro F1；在 policy optimization 与搜索任务中，包括 guided decoding 和 Best-of-N selection，PRISM 也持续提升准确率与鲁棒性，最高带来 22% guided decoding 提升和 33% Best-of-N 提升。
key_points_zh: 论文揭示 PRMs 的隐藏偏差：步骤级训练数据严重不均衡，加上标准 cross-entropy 训练，会让模型过度奖励貌似合理但错误的步骤。
作者强调 false positives 的危害大于 false negatives：前者会把 Best-of-N、guided decoding 和 policy optimization 主动导向错误推理。
PRISM 将 PRM 训练从逐点标签拟合转向可靠的相对比较，通过 contrastive step-level comparisons 学习更精确的步骤排序。
PRISM 使用 temporal lookahead 自动生成 hard negatives，不需要新增人工标注，并结合 difficulty-aware curriculum 调整对比 margin。
在 PRMBench、ProcessBench 及下游搜索/优化任务中，PRISM 显著降低 false positives，并提升 guided decoding、Best-of-N 等场景的准确率和鲁棒性。

llm_assessment.comment: PRISM is valuable for verifier-backed reasoning and reward reliability, though its contribution is mostly generic PRM training rather than agent-platform infrastructure.
llm_assessment.comment_zh: PRISM 对提升过程奖励与验证器可靠性有价值，但主要贡献仍是通用 PRM 训练，而非智能体平台基础设施。
